name: Halfback pass
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 35: Gadget plays: the wildcat, the halfback pass and the pitch
what: The halfback pass is a trick play where the running back throws the ball. The quarterback hands or pitches to the back, who starts running toward the sideline like a normal sweep.

The run fake does the work, just like play-action: the linebackers and a safety see a run and charge forward to stop it. Then the back stops behind the line of scrimmage and throws deep to a receiver who has slipped behind them. Any player can throw a forward pass, as long as it's from behind the line and it's the only forward pass of the play.

Coaches save it for big moments, like late in a close game, because it only works when the defense is playing the run hard. Its risks: the pitch is a backward pass, so a dropped pitch is a live fumble, and run-blocking linemen who drift downfield draw an ineligible-man-downfield flag.

caption: Dashed white: the quarterback's pitch to the running back and the back's deep throw. Solid white: the back's run toward the sideline and the receivers' routes. Yellow dashes: the linebacker, safety and cornerback coming up for the run.
spot: It starts like a sweep: a pitch or handoff to a back heading wide, with the line run blocking. Then the back pulls up short of the line and looks downfield. A receiver who seems to be blocking at first and then runs past the defense is the giveaway. Usually seen once in a game, if at all.
beats: Aggressive defenses whose linebackers and safeties race up to stop the run. Log it as a Pass in the drill: it is scored as a pass, so a pre-snap Run call will show as a miss; that's the trick working, so keep calling Run on those looks.
